label: rem:rieffel-metric-quotient-faithfulness
title: Rieffel Lipschitz seminorms, trace-radical descent, and quotient metric faithfulness
html:
The categorical Dirac operator \mathcal{D}_\nabla = q^{-1}\nabla + (1 - q^{-1})\iota_\xi\nabla combines horizontal covariant differentiation and Reeb contact transport with weights q^{-1} and 1 - q^{-1} summing to 1; for 1 < q both weights are strictly positive, making the induced transport cost anisotropic across horizontal and contact directions rather than a pure Reeb step count. On any unital K-algebra A over a strictly ordered field K, a first-order differential operator of this form induces a Lipschitz seminorm L \colon A \to K satisfying L(1_A) = 0, L(c a) = |c|\,L(a) for c \in K, and L(a + b) \le L(a) + L(b) [connes1989, connes1994, rieffel1999].

Dualising L across unital K-linear states \varphi, \psi \colon A \to K defines the Connes--Rieffel transport supremum

  d_L(\varphi, \psi)
  \;=\;
  \sup\{\,|\varphi(a) - \psi(a)| : a \in A,\; L(a) \le 1\,\},

which coincides on finite state graphs with the Kantorovich--Rubinstein optimal transport distance [kantorovich1942, rubinstein1957, rieffel2004]. Two structural properties link metric separation to algebraic indiscernibility in a quantum observable universe:

  1. Metric Identity of Indiscernibles. Zero dual bound d_L(\varphi, \psi) = 0 holds if and only if \varphi = \psi on all of A: elements with L(a) = 0 lie directly in the unit Lipschitz ball, while elements with L(a) > 0 enter after normalisation to L(a)^{-1} a.
  2. Trace-radical descent and scalar-kernel faithfulness. If L vanishes on a non-scalar element r \in A and two states satisfy \varphi(r) \neq \psi(r), arbitrary scalar multiples t r remain inside \{L \le 1\} while driving |\varphi(t r) - \psi(t r)| past every bound [rieffel1999]. In particular, whenever L vanishes on the null radical \mathrm{rad}\,\tau = \{r \in A : \tau(r b) = 0 \text{ for all } b \in A\} of a trace functional \tau, every pair of states at finite distance agrees identically on \mathrm{rad}\,\tau. Passing to the Gelfand--Naimark--Segal quotient A / \mathrm{rad}\,\tau [gelfand-naimark1943, segal1947] eliminates trace-indiscernible combinations, collapses \ker L to the scalar subalgebra K \cdot 1, and converts a degenerate seminorm into a faithful Kantorovich--Rubinstein metric on the quotient state space.
